claims.statement: DacExergy.carnot_in_mem_unit: for 0 < T0 < T, 0 < 1 - T0/T < 1 (heat supplied above ambient has an exergy weight in (0,1)); DacExergy.refrig_weight_lt_one: for 0 < T0 and T0/2 < T < T0, 0 < T0/T - 1 < 1 (rejecting heat just below ambient costs between 0 and 1 joule of work per joule). Real-number algebra; no thermodynamic content beyond the definitions of the two weights.

DacExergy.numerator_factor: q(T0/Tc - 1) - R(T0 - Tc) = (T0 - Tc)(q/Tc - R) for Tc != 0; co2_term_penalises_cold: if 0 < Tc < T0 and R Tc < q then -q(T0/Tc - 1) + R(T0 - Tc) < 0 (the CO2-only term of the exergy benefit is negative; NOT the sign of the whole benefit); co2_term_facevalue_favours_cold: 0 < R(T0 - Tc) for R > 0, Tc < T0; instance_r1: the displayed rational instance (R = 8.314, q = 40 kJ/mol, Tc = 200 K, T0 = 298.15 K) is negative (norm_num).

DacExergy.benefit_affine_in_r (a ring identity); worst_case_full_recovery: if 0 <= gam*D and r <= 1 then A + lam B <= A + lam B + (1-r) gam D (r = 1 is the worst case for a cold start when gam D >= 0); lambda_threshold_iff: for B > 0, 0 < A + lam B <-> -A/B < lam; threshold_iff: for 0 < R D, 0 < -N + gam (R D) <-> N/(R D) < gam. Pure algebra on real numbers.

DacExergy.wmin_pure_pos: R T0 log(1/x) > 0 for R, T0 > 0 and 0 < x < 1; wmin_pure_strictAnti: it is strictly decreasing in x on x > 0. These are statements about the function R T0 log(1/x), the minimum work to extract a pure component from an ideal mixture at mole fraction x; the identification with the physical minimum work is a (textbook) gloss, not a Lean statement.

Planted controls (formal_cert/Programmes/DacExergy/Controls.lean, never imported): ctl_sorry reports sorryAx and ctl_axiom reports DacExergy.ctl_cheat in #print axioms, although the file compiles with rc 0 (a compile exit code alone accepts both). The claim recorded is that the audit catches them. Filed A because it is a kernel-side fact about two named declarations.

McDannald, Siderius, DeCost, Choudhary, Ortiz-Montalvo, Intrinsic Direct Air Capture, arXiv:2501.04825v1 (8 Jan 2025): idealised piston with three steps; E1 = Q_ads - W1 (eq. 1), E2 = integral over a path s in (T,P) space (eqs. 2-4), E3 = 0 'no energy recovery' (eq. 5), E_total = E1 + E2 + E3 (eq. 6), purity (eq. 7), xi = dn_CO2/E_total (eq. 8), C = 1/xi (eq. 9), optimisation prior (eq. 10: T1 >= 200 K, dT ~ U(0,200), P1 ~ U(101325, 1.1*101325), dP ~ U(-101225, 0)); Table 2 (14 Pareto rows, xi in umol/J, printed values 6.12 to 11.259); statements on pp. 14-15 (heat recovery 'could therefore exceed our stated upper limit') and p. 22 (T1 lower limit 200 K). The supplement was NOT read.

Dataset Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14452152 (NIST Data Publication 10.18434/mds2-3687, version 1.0; authors McDannald and Siderius; licence CC-BY-4.0) and code NIST IntrinsicDACCycle v0.0.2 (Julia, NIST software licence: use, copy, distribute and modify with the notice kept; modified works carry a change notice; NIST must be acknowledged as source). DAC_data.tar.gz md5 a2520f520140c60f8a4663d5b403966c equals the Zenodo value; sha256 75a73c75a376a4611511af4a9e99b15af10096fa1886e5d969e4a1d8268df3fa.

The sentence on p. 20 of arXiv:2501.04825v1 as extracted from the PDF text reads 'There are a few sorbents with intrinsic capture efficiencies above 1.0 x 10^5 mol/J for their Pareto optimal paths' (the exponent is printed without a minus sign in the extraction, while the next sentence's 2.46 x 10^-6 keeps its minus). Text extraction only; the page image was not inspected by a person.

Stylised two-component surrogate (van 't Hoff Henry loadings for CO2 and N2, sensible heat c = gamma R n0, heat-recovery fraction r on the sensible heat; code/cert_sign.py docstring): the benefit of starting at Tc < T0 instead of T0, beta = C(T0) - C(Tc), equals A + lam B + (1-r) gamma R D with A_ex = -(T0-Tc)(q_C/Tc - R) and A_fv = R(T0-Tc). Consequences by the Lean algebra: A_ex < 0 whenever q_C > R Tc; beta is affine in r, so r = 1 is the worst case for cold when D >= 0; at r = 1 cold wins iff lam B > -A_ex, i.e. (B > 0 and) lam > lam* = (T0-Tc)(q_C/Tc - R)/B; for r < 1 the heat-capacity threshold gamma > N/((1-r) R D) with N = -(A + lam B). The derivation of the decomposition from the surrogate's definition is a hand argument; only the algebraic steps are in Lean.

In the surrogate, A_ex < 0 over the whole parameter box Tc in [200,272] K, T0 in [273,313] K, Th in [315,400] K, q_C in [12,67] kJ/mol (certified; trivially, since q_C >= 12000 J/mol exceeds R*272 K = 2261 J/mol).

Certified signs of the surrogate benefit beta at the stated numeric parameters of 164 parameter sets (data/logs/surrogate_params.json) x 3 ambient temperatures x 3 recovery fractions (those with Tc < T0 only: 155, 159, 162 sets at T0 = 273.15, 298.15, 313.15 K): at T0 = 298.15 K and r = 0, 151 positive (cold wins), 8 negative, 0 undecided (159 sets); at T0 = 298.15 K and r = 1, 131 positive, 28 negative. Outward-rounded mpmath interval arithmetic; the statement is about the surrogate evaluated at those numbers.

An independent plain-float implementation of the surrogate lies inside the interval enclosures for 2854 of 2856 points; the other 2 differ by 3e-8 relative from float cancellation, with the same sign. The first run of the surrogate lacked the factor R on the sensible term (1904 of 2856 mismatches), was found by this check, fixed and rerun.

Positive control: the Python re-implementation of the published energy balance (code/k1/dac_model.py) with the dataset reproduces Table 2 in 14 of 14 rows, 8 of 8 printed fields each, from the stored posterior statistics (PC-a); recomputes every stored nominal array and E_total with maximum normalised deviation 3.755e-11 (PC-b; one density per material back-solved from one stored number); nominal versus posterior-mean xi differs by -2.3 % to +1.3 % (PC-c, unseeded 100-draw posterior); re-fitted Cv within 4.0e-6 relative (PC-d).

Exergy re-accounting of the 14 stored Table 2 paths at T0 = 298.15 K (heats weighted by Carnot factors, works kept at face value, Step 3 priced): no-credit xi_NC (r = 0) 25.4 to 36.8 umol/J, against the face-value nominal recompute 5.98 to 11.26 umol/J (printed posterior means 6.12 to 11.259); reversible floor B_rev 25.0 to 27.0 kJ/mol against ideal-mixture W_min(P0, y) 18.8 to 19.4 kJ/mol (xi_rev 37.0 to 40.0 umol/J < 1/W_min); refrigeration is 47 to 80 % of the no-credit exergy cost.

Joint re-optimisation (grid plus refinement over T1, dT and P_end >= 100 Pa, P1 as stored) of the 14 Table 2 rows: the exergy-optimal T1 lies in 200 to 236.54 K in 14 of 14 rows in every one of 18 variants (T0 in {273.15, 298.15, 313.15} K x r in {0, 0.5, 1} x purity constraint on/off); 0 of 14 rows have T1* >= T0 in any variant; the face-value control puts all 14 optima below 273 K (maximum 231.98 K).

Cold-start benefit ratio (best xi with joint cold start / best xi with T1 >= 298.15 K, T0 = 298.15 K), 14 rows: face value 10.2 to 819; exergy r = 0: 3.5 to 129; r = 0.5: 2.6 to 80; r = 1: 1.25 to 6.6. Unconstrained optimal T_end: face value 227 to 400 K; exergy r = 0 301 to 340 K.

H2: over 8,765 materials with valid paths (15,161 paths; 11,656 optimised files in the public record), the published face-value xi never exceeds 1/W_min (dataset maximum 11.259 umol/J, VANNIK, against 51.6 umol/J). The reversible exergy floor B_rev falls below the ideal-mixture W_min (lowest-pressure bound) for 18 path/T0 pairs at 298.15 K (14 at 273.15 K, 21 at 313.15 K) in the 5 materials CSMNOX_clean, GUSNEN_SL, PACYIE_clean, SABWAU01_clean, UJOKIP05_clean at 298.15 K; most are degenerate paths (purity < 4 %, xi ~ 0), SABWAU01 (purity 0.91, B_rev = -42 J/mol) and UJOKIP05 (purity 0.67) are not. They are inconsistent inputs in those entries (for example extrapolated heats of adsorption). The h2_all.py counter skipped cases with W_min(low P) < 0 and reports fewer (2, 5); h2_violators.json is authoritative.

Slice scan on a seeded random sample of 150 materials (seed 20261027; best stored Pareto path of each; T_end, P1, P_end held): at T0 = 298.15 K and r = 0 the exergy optimum has T1* >= T0 in 3 of 150 (unconstrained). Re-selecting among all 15,161 stored Pareto paths of 8,765 materials, the no-credit-exergy-best path starts below 298.15 K for 8,420 of 8,765 materials (face value: 8,416). Conditional, not a re-optimisation.

Agreement of the surrogate sign (DAC-C-0003) with the full-model slice scan on the seeded 150-material sample at T0 = 298.15 K: 149/150 (r = 0), 146/150 (r = 0.5), 128/150 (r = 1). On the 14 Table 2 rows (paper-side recount, per path): r = 1 disagrees on 11 of 14 rows at T0 = 273.15 K, 10 of 13 scorable rows at 298.15 K and 5 of 8 at 313.15 K (the surrogate predicts cold loses; the full model says cold wins); at r = 0 all scorable rows agree. The interval statements are therefore about the surrogate only.

Controls: positive and negative. Positive: real BEVQID ledger passes the gate G1-G4; an all-T >= T0 path (min 300 K) has heat-in weights in (0,1), no refrigeration term, heat-out free; joint-scan face-value optimum reproduces 'start cold' (14/14 below 273 K); scan self-check <= 4.2e-7 relative. Negative, all rejected by the gate: double-counted sorbent heat (G2), planted x10^6 unit error (G4), the text's 1.0e5 mol/J taken literally (G4), heats of adsorption removed (G3: B_rev 8.7 kJ/mol < W_min 13.5 kJ/mol).

Unit observation: the dataset field Intrinsic_capture_efficiency carries the units string 'mol/J'; its maximum posterior value is 1.1259e-5 mol/J; 60 of the 8,765 materials have at least one path above 1.0e-5 mol/J; Table 2 prints xi in umol/J (maximum 11.259). The printed sentence (DAC-L-0003) is consistent with 1.0 x 10^-5 mol/J.

Neutral observations on the published code and data: unseeded 100-draw posterior; Cv drawn once per call so printed uncertainties omit Cv variability; Captured_CO2 is a posterior mean while E_Balance is nominal; three descriptions of the single path (text 250 to 350 K then 40,530 Pa; stored files and README 250 to 375 K and 42,844.84 Pa; code default 300 to 350 K); eight Table 2 rows with P1 in 82,466 to 101,126 Pa although eq. 10 and the v0.0.2 optimiser bound P1 to >= 101,325 Pa; nominal paths found by our grid with the published evaluator that exceed several Table 2 rows in both xi and purity (PARFOF 8.42 vs 5.98 umol/J at purity 0.99999; MAXHEA 8.62 vs 6.77; IFUDAO 8.60 vs 7.27), so the published front may not be fully converged (an observation to check, not a claim).

HEADLINE (negative result for our hypothesis). In the published simplified model, re-weighting every heat by its Carnot factor at an explicit ambient T0 and pricing Step 3 does NOT move the optimal start temperature to ambient or above for any of the 14 Table 2 rows (T1* 200 to 236.54 K in all 18 variants); the cold-start benefit ratio shrinks (face value 10 to 819 -> exergy r = 0 3.5 to 129 -> r = 1 1.25 to 6.6) but stays above 1. Our preregistered hypothesis H1 (the optimum moves to T1 >= T0 for most rows) is refuted. Thermodynamic limits of the published model only.

No output of any of these exists and none is claimed.
